why: The fix round's build after the plan's amendment of 2026-11-16 (docs/plan/quests/port-typecheck-PLAN.md, 'a dead .break is broken under its own .break'), in today's tooling. scripts/typecheck/LocksFile.ts: breakStale(path, withChild) now breaks a stale .break by calling itself on it, under .break.break, in place of removing it directly, as Mercurial 7.2.4's _testlock takes .break as a lock of its own with timeout=0; a .break, at any depth, is removed on the way out only while it still names this process (removeIfOurs, which release now shares); the wrong comment about two dead breakers is gone. The 8 hand _tag comparisons became the unions' matchers: LocksFile.ts failedWith uses Predicate.isTagged, the two .break checks and the hold loop use Seen.match, the look under .break uses Seen.guards.stale, Look.ts uses Liveness.match, Typecheck.ts uses Listing.guards.refused. NodeModulesFs.ts:20 stays, inside Effect.catchIf. One call taken at 85%: a stale .break whose own .break.break is held by a live breaker answers busy (the caller sleeps and tries again), not again as the plan's sketch wrote; that is what Mercurial's _testlock does when its inner lock is held (it returns the locker, read as held), and it avoids a loop with no sleep.

plants.plant: on the fixed code, the stale branch for a .break put back to fs.remove(breaker) then again: both B and C hold ([602, 603], expected length 1)
